newsitem.title: USA: Sun CEO hails turnaround at Northeast ops.
newsitem.headline: Sun CEO hails turnaround at Northeast ops.

text.p: Sun Co said Thursday that its first quarter earnings saw a turnaround in several of its operating units, particularly its struggling Northeast Refining division.

"Higher production levels, particularly of high-value fuels and chemicals products, and lower absolute costs resulted in significantly improved earnings from our Northeast refinery system, despite an overall refining environment that was weaker than the 1996 first quarter," Sun Chairman and Chief Executive Officer Robert H. Campbell in a statement.
Sun Northeast Refining reported operating income of $4 million in the first quarter of 1997 versus a loss of $28 million in the year-ago period.

Input to the crude units averaged over 479,000 barrels per day, or nearly 100 percent of rated capacity, and a decline in expenses of over $20 million pre-tax resulted in the significant improvement over prior year earnings, which had been hit by a high level of maintenance activity.
"We are on track with our plans to significantly improve production levels and reduce operating costs in Northeast Refining in 1997," Chief Operating Officer Jack Drosdick commented.

"Total production was up almost 5 million barrels versus the first quarter of 1996, and gasoline and distillate production averaged over 408,000 barrels daily, versus 358,000 in the first quarter of 1996," he said.
Operating costs were cut by about $15 million and total unit expenses by over $20 million, versus first quarter 1996 levels.
